messages:
maria: Customer on Private (vpc-prod-42) reporting intermittent inference timeouts to runtime on port 5100. Requests hang during TLS handshake, looks like SYNs are not getting a SYN/ACK.

maria: Example tcpdump from customer's app host:```
11:23:45.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 172.31.22.143.5100: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
11:23:45.223456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 172.31.22.143.5100: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
```

maria: curl to runtime returns TLS handshake timeout:```
$ curl -v https://172.31.22.143:5100/health
* Connected to 172.31.22.143 (172.31.22.143) port 5100 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
```

anshu: Thanks — first things: is there a customer-managed firewall or strict egress allowlist? NACLs are stateless so they often trip on return/ephemeral ports.

maria: Customer says egress policy only allows outbound to 80/443. Host-level egress to 0.0.0.0/0 is blocked.

anshu: That matches. Quick checks to run on customer host: `sudo tcpdump -n host 172.31.22.143 and port 5100`, `sudo iptables -S`, and run `traceroute -T -p 5100 172.31.22.143`. Can they also provide subnet NACL rules?

maria: They ran `traceroute -T -p 5100` — trace reaches the LB and then stops. They pasted their NACL rules.

infra-bot: alert: inference-port-5100 connection_error rate +320% between 11:20-11:40 — https://redwood.internal/alerts/12345

nick: Short checklist:
- SG on runtime instance: inbound TCP 5100 allowed from LB CIDR
- SG outbound is stateful (should allow return) but host firewall + customer firewall can block return traffic
- NACL on subnet must allow inbound/outbound for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) because NACLs are stateless

maria: Customer provided aws describe-network-acls output (acl-0abcde123). Important rules excerpt:```
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 5100 172.31.0.0/16
Rule 110: DENY TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0
Rule *: DENY ALL
```

anshu: Bingo — their NACL is explicitly denying ephemeral ports. Because NACLs are stateless you must allow the ephemeral range in both directions. Two remediation options:
1) Update the NACL to allow TCP 1024-65535 outbound/inbound for the relevant CIDRs.
2) Expand customer-managed firewall egress to include our runtime IPs and allow ephemeral return ports.
(Option 1 preferred given subnet-level control.)

maria: Suggested exact change to customer:```
# Add rule (e.g., 120) to NACL
120 ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0
# Keep 100 ALLOW TCP 5100 172.31.0.0/16
```

nick: Also verify host-level iptables. SGs are stateful so if inbound 5100 is allowed and host OS allows outbound ephemeral, it should work. But if the customer has a middlebox that blocks ephemeral ports, they need to change that too.

jess: (on call with customer) applied NACL update: removed DENY for 1024-65535 and added explicit allow for return traffic. Re-testing now.

maria: Re-running curl:```
$ curl -v https://172.31.22.143:5100/health
* Connected to 172.31.22.143 (172.31.22.143) port 5100 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

jess: Customer confirms inference requests now succeed and latency returned to baseline.

maria: Closing loop — added note to triage checklist: when TLS handshake/timeouts happen on non-443 inference ports check NACL deny for ephemeral ports and customer egress allowlist. cc @anshu @nick :thumbsup: 

nick: Great. Please add a KB entry with the NACL snippet and tcpdump troubleshooting steps, then mark the ticket resolved.

anshu: +1, also add an example `tcpdump` and `traceroute -T -p` snippet to the KB.

maria: Will write the KB and attach the customer's NACL excerpt (redacted).
